idiom_name: case class with member methods and a smart constructor
implementation_notes: The classic Scala realization keeps the concept as a case class whose member methods enforce the invariants, with a private primary constructor plus a companion apply that validates, because copy and unapply expose the representation; transforming operations return a new instance and therefore another concept (Closure of Operations). Choose it when the behaviour is intrinsic to the type and clients are expected to call it directly.
pitfalls: Case classes are open: copy and pattern matching expose the representation, so invariants must be re-established in every construction path (private constructor + validating companion apply).
Putting every helper method on the case class eventually makes it a god class; methods that only use the public API belong in extensions or a companion.

variants.name: Extension methods on a data type (Scala 3)
variants.idiom_name: case class as data + extension methods for behaviour
variants.implementation_notes: Scala 3 lets one keep the data declaration minimal and add the operations afterwards with extension methods (replacing Scala 2's implicit classes), which separates data from behaviour and lets a caller import exactly the operations it uses; a given instance can also carry the extensions so they are available in the type's implicit scope. Choose it when the operation is not essential to the type, when the type is closed (a library or generated class), or when different layers should see different behaviour on the same data.
pitfalls: Extension methods resolve statically on the declared type and must be imported (or in implicit scope), so a change of import can silently switch or hide an operation.
Extensions cannot see private members: logic that needs the representation stays in the class or forces visibility open, which weakens the contour it was meant to protect.
